videos.title: Fixture: Postgres indexes in fifteen minutes
videos.transcript: Welcome back. Today we look at indexes in Postgres. A B-tree index keeps keys sorted, which serves equality and range lookups. A GIN index maps each element of a composite value, such as the keys of a JSONB document, to the rows that contain it. An index costs write time and disk space, so add one when a query needs it, and check with EXPLAIN that the planner uses it.
videos.summary:
## Overview

A short tour of the index types Postgres offers and when each pays off.

## B-tree

The default. It keeps keys sorted and serves equality and range conditions.

## GIN

Indexes the elements of composite values, for example the keys of a JSONB column.

## Costs

Every index slows writes and takes disk space; `EXPLAIN` shows whether the planner uses it.

key_points: B-tree serves equality and range lookups
GIN indexes the elements of JSONB and arrays
Each index costs write time and disk space
action_items: Run EXPLAIN on the slowest query before adding an index

videos.title: Fixture: Context cancellation in Go
videos.transcript: A context carries a deadline and a cancellation signal across API boundaries. Pass it as the first argument. Derive a child with WithTimeout when a call needs its own limit, and always call the cancel function. A goroutine that ignores ctx.Done keeps running after its caller has given up.
videos.summary:
## Overview

How `context.Context` carries deadlines and cancellation through a Go program.

## Rules

- Pass the context as the first argument.
- Derive a child with `WithTimeout` for a call with its own limit.
- Call the cancel function, also on the success path.

## Pitfall

A goroutine that does not select on `ctx.Done()` outlives its caller.

key_points: Every derived context has a cancel function that must be called

videos.title: Fixture: Sourdough starter from scratch
videos.transcript: Mix equal weights of flour and water. Keep it warm. Every day discard half and feed it again with equal weights. After about a week it doubles within six hours of a feed, and then it is ready to bake with.
videos.summary:
## Overview

A starter needs flour, water, warmth and a week of daily feeding.

## Method

Equal weights of flour and water; discard half and feed daily.

## Ready when

It doubles within about six hours after a feed.

key_points: Equal weights of flour and water
Ready when it doubles within six hours
action_items: Feed the starter at the same time every day

videos.title: Fixture: Vortrag über Wärmepumpen
videos.transcript: Eine Wärmepumpe hebt Wärme aus der Umgebung auf ein höheres Temperaturniveau. Je geringer die Vorlauftemperatur, desto höher die Jahresarbeitszahl. Große Heizflächen erlauben eine niedrige Vorlauftemperatur.
videos.summary:
## Overview

The talk explains how a heat pump works and what decides its efficiency.

## Efficiency

The lower the flow temperature, the higher the seasonal performance factor; large radiators allow a low flow temperature.

key_points: Radiator area decides the flow temperature

videos.title: Fixture Weekly 101: Backups that restore
videos.transcript: HOST: This week, backups. GUEST: A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a backup. Schedule a restore test, measure how long it takes, and write the steps down while you do it.
videos.summary:
## Overview

The hosts argue that a backup counts only once it has been restored.

## Advice

- Schedule regular restore tests.
- Measure the restore time.
- Write the restore steps down during the test.

key_points: An untested backup is not a backup
Restore time is a number to measure
